lantern_lu_han.name: Lu Han
lantern_lu_han.title: Paid relay porter with an ordinary receiving shift

lantern_04_001.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_001.text: Jin Lu opened the fuel cabinet on Day 1411 while Ma counted the locked issue trays. The little stone cells stood in padded rows, their ceramic caps dull beneath the workroom lamp. Yue had expected a more impressive light. Most of the charge remained inside its rated casing and showed nothing a visitor could usefully admire. Jin gave her the public counting sheet. One hundred and twenty cells remained from the initial accepted one hundred and sixty after thirty-six transmission windows and four licensed bench portions.

lantern_04_002.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_002.text: The cabinet door had swollen during the damp week. A porter had pushed it closed with his shoulder, leaving a shallow scrape along the upper row's padded rail. Jin stopped the count when she found two cap seals lifting at their edges. She did not ask Yue to press them flat. The cells went into rated isolation supports under the examiner's handling plan. Their charge remained externally contained, but their present seals failed the issue condition. One hundred and eighteen usable cells stayed in the operating count; two suspect cells remained separately listed.

lantern_04_003.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_003.text: Ma swore when she saw the porter mark on the door. The porter, Lu Han, stood beside the public threshold with his hands inside his sleeves. He had closed the door after a normal evening issue and had not seen a damaged cap. He wanted the failed cells charged to his wages before the whole desk learned of it. Jin said the cause required examination. The scrape showed contact with a rail. It did not date the seal defect or establish how much his shoulder had contributed. Ma sent him to fetch the actual closing log.

lantern_04_004.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_004.text: The log recorded a sticking door on three previous evenings. The first porter had reported it to the maintenance tray; the second had copied the report; Lu had asked whether the door was still admitted. The acting desk had answered yes without a cabinet inspection. Deng read those lines and put her own initials beside the missed follow-up. Lu's ordinary wage would be paid. The door needed an assigned repair, and the failed seals needed their own cause review. A worker's ready shame could not supply either result.

lantern_04_005.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_005.text: Fen Tao inspected the hinge and found wet wood pressing the door against its frame. She could adjust the ordinary fit without touching charged cells. Jin isolated the cabinet stock while Fen worked. Yue helped Ma move the public queue board to a different clear wall because the repair space occupied its usual corner. Senders gathered around the new position with the familiar impatience of people whose paper had become difficult to find. Lu guided them himself, quieter than yesterday but still knowing which desk could answer each question.

lantern_04_006.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_006.text: The fuel supplier's representative arrived with the new order's advance notice before the hinge work ended. His name was Bei Rong, and he wore a coat whose sleeves had been polished smooth by counters. The association's four hundred and twenty copper ordered two hundred and ten compatible external cells at two each, with condition checks at Chime before acceptance. He wanted the full amount released against his warehouse count. Deng refused because the agreed price included accepted condition at destination. Bei said the difference would delay his own supplier payment.

lantern_04_007.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_007.text: Jin asked him to inspect the two lifted seals within the permitted comparison. He admitted the visible defect and checked their maker marks. They came from the earlier accepted batch, still inside its stated defect review period. He could submit a claim under that actual warranty, not promise replacements before the maker's answer. Deng gave him the condition record. He kept its offered technical fields and left Lu's unrelated wage history off the copy. Lu watched the two cases separate on the table and finally took his hands out of his sleeves.

lantern_04_008.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_008.text: The door repair finished before the afternoon window. Fen tested its ordinary movement after Jin confirmed the stock's supported clearance. It opened without scraping the upper rail. Deng paid the accepted small repair from the building's existing maintenance account, whose local clerk supplied the available balance and receipt. It did not come from the proposed fuel purchases or Yue's wages. Ma added the actual cabinet check to the evening closing task. The next porter would see the earlier unresolved report and the completed repair, rather than inherit a silence somebody hoped had ended.

lantern_04_009.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_009.text: That evening, Pu An received the roof order's last invoice payment. He counted it beside the little toy-pot lid and bought the ordinary visiting ticket he had hoped to afford. His daughter lived at East Sill, one of the relay's actual receiving points. He wanted to travel there himself on Day 1415, when his employer had approved an afternoon away. The current market cart could take him at the accepted rate. The relay could carry a paid message announcing his visit; it could not move his body into her doorway.

lantern_04_010.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_010.text: Yue asked whether he wanted help wording the message. He wanted to write it himself. The first draft promised a whole day, and he crossed that out after checking the ticket's real return. His daughter would have an afternoon. He included the promise to bring the lid and ask what game her toy pot played now. Yue left him alone with the final line. He was not ashamed of the narrow visit. He wanted it to be true enough that a child could wait for its actual beginning.

lantern_04_011.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_011.text: On Day 1412, Jin released the first day's fuel use to the public summary. Four admitted windows and one bench portion had consumed five cells, leaving one hundred and thirteen usable. The two suspect cells remained in isolation. Ma copied the number onto the issue board, then erased an old proposed purchase quantity a porter had written beside it. The new order had not arrived. A sender reading the board needed today's available supply, rather than a promise occupying the same line as charged cells.

lantern_04_012.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_012.text: The first morning window carried Pu's message under his paid sending terms. East Sill's receiving clerk signed its actual local receipt through the admitted return channel. The clerk would deliver it to the household under the ordinary post route; that last step remained pending. Pu wanted to mark the toy lid packed as soon as the receipt arrived. Yue laughed and asked whether packing the lid depended on his daughter reading the note. It did not. He wrapped it now, then went to his own paid workshop.

lantern_04_013.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_013.text: Bei Rong returned with an offer for a cheaper substitute cell. Its maker claimed a longer duration in a different cradle. Jin read the public rating and found that it did not certify Chime's compatible input or independent stop. A bench comparison would need a separately authorised test within her equipment's limits. Deng had purchased compatible cells, and the supplier could not fill the missing order with an attractive label. Bei called the refusal conservative. Jin asked which actual measurement made the substitute compatible. He had none.

lantern_04_014.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_014.text: Lu Han heard the exchange and became angry on Jin's behalf. She told him to continue the queue task. Bei's opinion did not change the instrument's rating, and public indignation would not inspect the proposed cells. Yue watched Lu return to senders with his old briskness restored. He could help the institution by doing the work he knew, rather than defending every examiner with a speech. The supplier left his substitute brochure behind. Deng kept it with the declined offer, where it could explain why the cheaper price had not been chosen.

lantern_04_015.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_015.text: At the cheaper house, Yue found Pu fitting the toy lid badly into its paper wrap. The round edge tore through one corner. She offered her remaining plain paper strip, and he bought an ordinary protective box from the nearby stall because the paper alone could not support it. The box cost a little more than he liked. He paid anyway. The lid's journey now had a physical support instead of an increasingly elaborate knot. Yue repaired the torn wrapper for her own dried greens, keeping the objects' needs separate.

lantern_04_016.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_016.text: Her local duty period on Day 1413 concerned a missing receiving interval at Moss Ford. A clerk there had changed shifts after a household birth, and the old notice still named his former hours. The replacement worker had accepted the defined cover under Moss Ford's own wage account. Ma needed the actual corrected hours before admitting the next household packets. Yue copied them from the permitted reply and sent the public proof to that desk. The new child's private details stayed outside the service change, leaving the clerk free to announce them himself.

lantern_04_017.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_017.text: Zheng came to the public walk carrying no lens case. He had wanted to see the cabinet repair but missed it while attending a household care appointment. Yue described the offered public result. He was annoyed at the wet hinge because he remembered advising an earlier manager to move the cabinet away from that wall. His old note might still exist in an admitted maintenance file. Deng would need to find it before calling the current fault a ignored warning. Zheng sighed at the slower answer and said he would look for his own permitted copy first.

lantern_04_018.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_018.text: Bao brought him home before the lunch pot emptied. He resented the reminder, then ate enough that the resentment seemed poorly founded. Yue stayed for the invited meal and heard the two argue about his old work coat. Bao wanted to patch its shoulder; Zheng wanted to keep the visible tear because it proved the coat had seen things. She asked whether cloth needed to prove history by admitting rain. He laughed and gave her the coat. Its old marks could survive an ordinary patch if somebody first decided which marks they actually wanted.

lantern_04_019.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_019.text: The failed cells' maker answered on Day 1414. It accepted examination under the stated warranty but required controlled discharge before the casings travelled for its material review. Jin would perform that work in the rated isolation bench, with charge not credited back to the usable inventory. Bei wanted to call the two replacements already supplied because the maker had approved the claim. Deng kept them pending until arrival. The two damaged cells had real charge that could no longer serve Chime's windows. No favourable letter made that capacity available again.

lantern_04_020.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_020.text: Jin carried out the controlled discharge with the ordinary appointed bench assistant. Yue copied only the admitted public condition summary afterward. The failed cap material would travel cold in its supports. Lu watched from the safe side when Jin showed him the emptied issue mark. The discharge had completed a dangerous object's permitted stop, while the cause remained under review. He asked whether he ought to apologise to the supplier. Jin said he could report exactly what he had done. An apology could be personal; it could not establish the defect's age.

lantern_04_021.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_021.text: Ma reduced an optional bench demonstration before the next shift, preserving operating fuel while the compatible order travelled. The cancelled demonstration had its own accepted visitor appointment. She contacted that visitor through the actual receiving address and returned the unspent demonstration fee. The visitor had already booked a ground cart to Chime and asked about its cancellation cost. Deng referred the documented cost to the association's review procedure, which had a limited ground-alternative balance. The fuel shortage had acquired a person and a bill, rather than staying a smaller number on Jin's slate.

lantern_04_022.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_022.text: The visitor was an ordinary school instructor from Ring Meadow. He wanted the demonstration because pupils had been treating pictures of the lamp as explanations of its machinery. He was angry at the cancellation and still agreed that a public lesson should not consume uncertain spare fuel. Deng offered an admitted cold-assembly explanation during a later date if he wanted one. It would answer different questions. He asked for the actual proposal before accepting and retained his existing travel-cost claim. A useful alternative did not erase the first loss.

lantern_04_023.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_023.text: On Day 1415, Pu left for East Sill on the actual booked market cart. Yue saw him holding the little supported box upright beside his ordinary lunch packet. His daughter's household had received the message and sent an acceptance through its own permitted reply. She wanted to show him a game involving a pebble soup that refused to boil. He had written that he was ready for difficult soup. The employer's approved visiting interval stayed on the workshop calendar. Neither the lamp nor a friendly colleague needed to hide his absence.

lantern_04_024.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_024.text: The fuel convoy's driver arrived first with the route report. A lower bridge inspection had admitted her loaded cart after an extra ordinary halt. The cells would reach Chime on Day 1416 if the last approach passed its morning check. Bei Rong wanted Deng to announce the arrival because the convoy was now close. Ma posted the actual expected date and the inspection condition instead. The public notice named the limited usable stock remaining. It supplied no false emergency, but it allowed senders to understand why optional demonstrations had stopped.

lantern_04_025.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_025.text: Rui sent a plain home-arrival line through the ordinary route she had booked. She had returned the rejected cloth samples, settled the finite travel allowance, and begun the school's accepted order under its own workshop contracts. Yue read the offered personal greeting and put it beside her unsent reply. Their short acquaintance had survived as actual correspondence. She wanted to answer without enclosing another institutional comparison. Rui had asked whether the tinsmith's lid reached his daughter. Yue could ask Pu when he returned, if he wanted to share that story.

lantern_04_026.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_026.text: The market cart brought Pu home before the employer's accepted return time. His daughter had tried the lid on the toy pot and found it too tight after putting a cloth under it. Pu showed her how to use the pot without the extra cloth, then listened when she explained that the cloth represented steam. He had taken the lid back only after she asked for a wider rim. The gift's first fitting had failed, and their afternoon had been good anyway. He would remake it from his own scrap, preserving the game instead of defending the measurement.

lantern_04_027.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_027.text: On Day 1416, the fuel cart passed the last approach check and reached the association's ordinary unloading bay. Bei Rong presented two hundred and ten cells. Jin admitted their supported unloading into the inspection room and kept them out of the issue cabinet until the current checks. The driver had transported a counted load, which deserved its own completed carriage payment whether or not the maker's cells all passed. Deng signed the actual arrival reference and let the driver leave after the load handover. The cargo's acceptance belonged to a different qualified worker.

lantern_04_028.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_028.text: Twenty-four cells failed the compatibility comparison. Their marker glaze matched the order, but their measured stop response exceeded Chime's admitted condition. Jin repeated the permitted control with a known compatible reference before rejecting them. The reference behaved within its recorded limit. Bei said the rejected cells could still carry plenty of charge. They could. Chime needed compatible external charge with an independent stop, not merely a convincing quantity trapped behind the right colour. Jin recorded the actual measurements and prohibited their issue to the old cradle.

lantern_04_029.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_029.text: Deng accepted one hundred and eighty-six cells under the agreed price, paying three hundred and seventy-two copper against that actual receipt. Forty-eight remained reserved for twenty-four accepted replacements. The two earlier warranty replacements remained a separate uncharged obligation. Bei wanted the association to keep all the new cells while the matter was argued. Jin permitted isolated custody under a defined return arrangement, with no usable-stock credit for the failed twenty-four. The paid cells entered their supported cabinet places only after the operator completed the count.

lantern_04_030.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_030.text: The usable inventory at the close of Day 1416 was two hundred and seventy-eight cells. One hundred and eighteen had remained after the first two failed seals were excluded; six days' twenty-four transmissions and two bench portions left ninety-two. The accepted one hundred and eighty-six supplied the actual addition. Ma read the number with Jin and the issue assistant, then moved to tomorrow's schedule. There was fuel to operate the current term. The rejected batch still threatened later provision and had exposed how much the cabinet depended on its maker's real work.

lantern_04_031.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_031.text: Bei Rong asked Yue privately whether the public note needed the word rejected. He feared it would cost his warehouse other orders before the maker could answer. Yue referred the question to Deng and Jin, whose actual accounts supplied the public fields. They retained the compatibility failure and the maker's pending response without calling every cell defective. Bei wanted an easier sentence. Deng wanted a sentence senders could use. They agreed on the current measured result and the exact subset. The note protected no general reputation at the expense of Chime's actual limit.

lantern_04_032.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_032.text: The maker's reply arrived with an uncomfortable admission. It had sent a variant lot after its usual ceramic stock ran short, relying on the glaze mark and warehouse record to distinguish them. The dispatch crew had treated the shared colour as the order category. The variant could have lawful uses elsewhere under its own rating, but not this accepted contract. Bei had known the ordinary stock was low and had not told Deng before seeking full payment. He brought the reply himself and did not try to blame the convoy's extra halt.

lantern_04_033.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_033.text: Deng asked him what he could actually supply by the next dated receiving review. He could obtain twenty-four compatible replacement cells and the two approved warranty cells from another listed warehouse, subject to its inspected stock and ordinary carrier. The maker would pay the extra replacement carriage under the agreed defect terms. The proposed arrival was Day 1423. Jin requested the warehouse's compatible lot record before loading. Bei agreed and wrote the named keeper's address. A cause had been established enough to choose a corrective action, while the action still had to travel.

lantern_04_034.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_034.text: Ma checked the ground-alternative account for the cancelled school instructor's actual cart cost. The instructor had submitted the unused reservation and cancellation charge. Its admitted five-copper cost met the association's defined review rule, and Deng approved that amount from the two-hundred-and-ten line. The instructor received the payment through his named local desk, with an actual signature. He kept his right to decline the proposed cold demonstration. Chime had repaired one specific cost of its cancellation without purchasing the teacher's gratitude or pretending his original lesson had happened.

lantern_04_035.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_035.text: Yue went to Shao Ye's preliminary registry appointment that afternoon, outside her local duty period. Shao read the prior certificate under the admitted receiving process and asked about the actual stopped form Yue had used. Yue described the half-unit input over four ordinary breaths, quarter-unit useful output, independent stop, and full grounded release. She described no fresh arrival reserve reading. Shao wanted the distinction kept on the first practice page. The possible great circuit would test a different internal arrangement, and would not retest every external task simply because its stage was higher.

lantern_04_036.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_036.text: The curriculum's minimum usable reserve stood at eighty-four after the registered recovery and sampling sequence. Its compatibility minimum stayed ninety-two percent. Shao required three separately dated recovered interrupted trials and each next-day tissue check, following prerequisite practice, failed-work review, and recovery. The current local bench provision could fund only the initial comparison and a small set of prepared tests. Further compatible cells, inspected support, and care needed their own actual source before the full curriculum could proceed. The public promise of instruction had an underfunded inventory Yue would have to face.

lantern_04_037.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_037.text: Yue had hoped her prior certificate would make the next registration simpler. It made the examiner's questions more exact. Shao showed her the actual paid tuition quote and the unfunded bench portion rather than concealing it in a generous invitation. Yue could defer without losing her existing stage. She could seek an ordinary training grant under the town's limited scheme. Her current wages were committed under an eighteen-day appointment, not yet all received and free to spend twice. She took the proposal home and began with its actual numbers.

lantern_04_038.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_038.text: Pu was widening the toy lid when she arrived. He asked whether the next examination had gone well. She said it had become possible to describe how it might go, which was less exciting. He laughed and offered the safe blunt edge of the old lid as a paper weight. His daughter had told him to keep it because it belonged to the first version of their soup. Yue used it on the tuition proposal with his permission. A failed gift could support a new question without being declared restored to the use it had not fitted.

lantern_04_039.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_039.text: The next morning brought a storm that could not have read the supplier's promised date. Wind drove rain against the tower's western shutters, and Jin closed the exposed viewing walk while the building keeper checked its fastening. The relay's current windows continued only through their admitted sheltered path. Yue crossed the public yard beneath her patched cloak, feeling the new seam hold while her ordinary shoes soaked. Ma stood at the queue with wet hair against her cheek. A sender wanted the lamp to hurry because his own road had become unpleasant.

lantern_04_040.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_040.text: He was carrying a request for his daughter's medicine from East Sill's dispensary. The request had its proper clinical receiver and offered fields, but the next relay window was not an emergency transport service. Ma could admit the message to the current window or quote an ordinary ground route whose timing differed. The sender chose the window after calling the dispensary through its actual enquiry arrangement. The dispenser would prepare the order if its clinician approved it. A light carried words; another person still had to prepare and carry medicine.

lantern_04_041.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_041.text: Yue saw the sender return before lunch, furious because the dispensing cart could not reach Chime that afternoon. East Sill's clinic had received the request and approved the named preparation, but the cart road was restricted by the storm. Ma gave him the actual reply and the ordinary local care address. The message had worked while the needed object remained elsewhere. He accused her of selling an empty service. She stayed at the desk long enough to answer the factual question, then asked the duty clerk to cover her next break.

lantern_04_042.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_042.text: Behind the partition, Ma pressed a dry cloth against her eyes without crying. She had a sister in Chime who always asked whether the lamp made her important. "Today it makes me the person standing here," she said. Yue asked whether she wanted company or quiet. Ma wanted the cloth wrung out and returned, then quiet until the appointed break ended. Yue did that ordinary task and went back to her own page. The four-hour documentary post had supplied no skill that could soothe every person whose necessary parcel waited beyond bad weather.

lantern_04_043.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_043.text: The local clinic saw the child that afternoon under its normal appointment process. Her parent gave Ma a brief permitted update: they had received local care while the East Sill order waited. He did not withdraw his complaint about the service description. Ma accepted both facts. Deng asked the public desk to make the distinction between transmission and transport clearer on its next price notice. The child did not become well because the institution improved its wording. Her care belonged to clinicians and the household, while the description belonged to the people who sold the message service.

lantern_04_044.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_044.text: Yue completed the public wording draft during her accepted duty period. The new line named transmission between receiving points and separate physical carriage afterward. She did not add the child's story to make the explanation persuasive. Ma checked the draft, then put it aside for the authorised price review. In the yard, the building keeper had found a shutter hinge that needed ordinary oiling and no structural replacement. Rain continued. Its smaller result gave Jin a safe viewing-walk reopening question for a later dry interval, rather than an instant end to the weather.

lantern_04_045.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_045.text: On Day 1418, Ma took an accepted afternoon off to watch her nephew's school play. The appointed relief dispatcher had already accepted the paid cover on the regional rota. Yue saw Ma remove her desk badge and put it in the proper drawer before leaving. She had sewn a paper fish for the performance, and its tail stuck out of her ordinary bag. The nephew, Yan Di, had complained that everybody in his family made fish because the school already knew enough foxes. Ma intended to applaud whatever animal he actually chose.

lantern_04_046.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_046.text: Yue stayed at the ordinary documentary desk because her own duty period had not ended. A sender arrived asking for Ma personally. The relief dispatcher could receive the offered message under the same current authority. The sender wanted a familiar face and waited until he understood the actual choice. He accepted the admitted desk rather than postponing his own packet. Yue watched the relief worker complete the count without Ma hidden behind a curtain. A staffed institution had made one person's afternoon possible through somebody else's real paid work.

lantern_04_047.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_047.text: Ma returned after the play with a damp paper tail and an indignant account of an elephant. Yan Di had decided the fish was too small to hold his question and had asked the teacher for a larger animal. The elephant wanted a pond delivered to its bedroom. Everybody in the room knew ponds could not travel that way, which made its argument louder. Ma had laughed until her stomach hurt. She left the tail on her own household shelf at work, far from the issued message forms, and asked Yue whether the ordinary queue had survived her absence.

lantern_04_048.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_048.text: Zheng read the supplier's public account from Bao's admitted copy. He wanted to visit Bei Rong and ask why a colour had become a measurement. Bao said he could ask the question at the public review, but should first remember the mislabeled practice parts he had once sent to an apprentice. Zheng looked offended, then began laughing slowly. His own old error had cost a paid return journey and an entire morning's fit test. Remembering it did not excuse Bei's choice. It changed the speech Zheng wanted to make, which had previously begun with fools.

lantern_04_049.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_049.text: He found the old cabinet note in his permitted correspondence box on Day 1419. It described damp wood and advised a hinge check before the wet period, without predicting failed cap seals. He offered its relevant passage to Deng for the cause review. Deng compared it with the admitted maintenance file and found the original had been received, then filed under exterior cupboards. The cabinet was inside the technical room. A classification error had helped the report wait in the wrong pile. It was a smaller and more useful explanation than saying the institution never listened.

lantern_04_050.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_050.text: Lu Han visited Zheng's room after his ordinary shift because he wanted to apologise for the shoulder push. Zheng asked him to describe the sticking door first. Lu did, with his hands illustrating the movement against an imagined frame. Bao made him stop before he knocked her sewing lamp. Zheng showed him the old note's limits. He had warned about damp fit, not inspected today's cap seals. Lu could regret a hurried movement without accepting every later fault as his own. Their conversation ended with Bao asking both men to carry the used bowls to the kitchen.

lantern_04_051.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_051.text: Yue's training proposal lay beneath Pu's first toy lid for two evenings before she reopened it. The initial tuition quote was twenty-four copper for the defined preregistration and supervised preparation block. A separate twelve-copper minimum bench provision was not yet assigned in the town's training fund. Later recovered trial costs would need a fresh reviewed allocation. Her existing stage certificate remained valid within its earlier named limits. She could pay the tuition after the local term settled, but paying it would not produce the missing compatible bench cells by itself.

lantern_04_052.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_052.text: She wrote a grant request using her actual current wages and the proposed curriculum. The scheme asked why the trained task would have local use. Yue wanted to say the lamp needed her, then stopped. The lamp used external fuel and appointed operators, and its retirement question belonged to them. Her controlled great circuit could qualify her for particular bounded comparisons if they were later inspected and offered. She described those possible tasks plainly. The clerk would decide among actual applications, including people whose ambitions she would never meet.

lantern_04_053.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_053.text: The cooperative's proofs contained an actual error in a cloth length on Day 1413. Yue compared the merchant's admitted original before returning it for correction, rather than guessing which number sold more cloth. Nine working afternoons from Day 1411 through Day 1420 produced twenty-seven additional accepted sheets, three each. Day 1416 remained the agreed rest date. On Day 1420 Suan paid fifty-four copper for those received pages, bringing the ongoing order's personal payments to one hundred ten. Its remaining proofs stayed unaccepted work, not cash she could spend.

lantern_04_054.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_054.text: On Day 1420, the cancelled instructor declined the proposed cold demonstration date. His school had arranged a local ordinary equipment lesson that did not require another journey to Chime. Deng recorded the refusal and retained the completed five-copper travel-cost payment. The association did not count a demonstration that had never been accepted. Ma put the freed meeting room back on its ordinary booking list. A local choir took the afternoon place at its normal rate and spent most of the first hour arguing over which pitch the room's echo made comfortable.

lantern_04_055.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_055.text: Yue checked the received money before paying the week's room charge. Her cheaper room had been booked from Day 1412 at one and a half copper nightly, with ordinary food budgeted separately at one copper daily. The former inn still held her last bedding under its already paid storage arrangement; that did not buy another occupied room. Two-hour proofreading afternoons had ended before dinner, leaving time for meals and sleep. The private job paid for actually checked merchandise information, and no customer acquired a favorable cultivation result through that fee.

lantern_04_056.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_056.text: Jin received the replacement warehouse's lot record that evening. It matched the compatible order category and named twenty-four contract replacements plus two warranty cells. She compared the offered rating with Chime's admitted reference, then requested the actual departure count. The record improved confidence in the proposed shipment. It did not put twenty-six cells in her cabinet. Ma retained the current usable count and schedule. Their remaining stock covered the accepted term, but the next appropriation's proposal would have to include the supplier's failure and the service lost when optional demonstrations stopped.

lantern_04_057.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_057.text: At the public cause review on Day 1421, Bei Rong admitted withholding the stock change before asking full payment. Lu Han described the door push. Deng described the misfiled old maintenance note. Jin supplied the current measured failures and the limit of the cause findings. Their accounts did not fuse into one person guilty of everything. The representatives required the supplier's dispatch category correction and the association's actual cabinet follow-up. Lu's wages stayed paid. Deng's own handling error remained in the minute, where public respect for her work could not erase it.

lantern_04_058.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_058.text: Zheng spoke briefly after the offered technical account. He told his old apprentice-part story instead of the speech about fools. Bei seemed annoyed to receive an imperfect fellow worker's recognition rather than an easy condemnation to resist. Zheng did not forgive the unannounced variant order on behalf of its owners. He asked Bei to send the actual replacement date to Ma before making another promise at a counter. Bei said he would. Bao took her uncle home afterward, making him eat before he tried to improve the whole meeting in another letter.

lantern_04_059.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_059.text: The replacement convoy left its warehouse on Day 1422 with its counted compatible lot and the maker-funded extra carriage. Ma received the actual dispatch reference through the ordinary route. The driver had not yet passed the last approach inspection, and the expected arrival remained conditional on it. Yue copied the public date into the accepted service note. She had now seen a proposed shipment, a counted departure, and a pending arrival. lantern_04_060.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_060.text: Yue moved the last of her own bedding into the cheaper room that afternoon. lantern_04_061.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_061.text: On Day 1423, Jin accepted the twenty-six replacement cells after their supported arrival and current compatibility checks. lantern_04_062.speaker: narrator

lantern_04_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_063.text: The local term ended on Day 1424. Four actual windows left two hundred and seventy usable fuel cells after the preceding evening's accepted replacements. lantern_04_064.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_064.text: After settling the local term, Yue paid the completed lodging balance and reserved a modest personal amount for the next ordinary days. She kept the twenty-four-copper tuition quote open pending the actual grant answer and bench provision.

lantern_04_065.speaker: narrator
lantern_04_065.text: Pu's wider toy lid now fitted his daughter's cloth steam, according to her household reply. He placed the first lid back beneath Yue's paper with a smile.
